writeup: Astronomers have identified a new eclipsing binary star system called TIC 295373509, which had never been cataloged before. The system completes one full orbit every 5.4 days, and observers detect a primary eclipse where the star dims by 8.03 percent as one object passes in front of the other. The secondary eclipse, where the companion would cross in front, has not been detected. The discovery was validated through multiple independent methods: a strong detection signal of 246.8 in the initial analysis, plus pixel-level imaging that confirmed the eclipse signature with high confidence. The candidate passed all data quality checks, making it a robust addition to our catalog of known binary star systems.
